title: Chapter 25: Distributed Delivery and Professional Capstone
description: Integrate the academy into an operable portfolio service. Learners version APIs, process duplicate messages idempotently, use outbox and saga patterns where their failure model requires them, bound caches, package a non-root container, implement readiness and graceful shutdown, define logs/metrics/traces and SLOs, execute safe rollouts, review unfamiliar code, and defend the capstone architecture from requirement through incident response.

exercises.title: Chapter 25 implementation lab: readiness
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Implement `readiness`. Return READY only when database and queue are true and shuttingDown is false; otherwise NOT_READY. Write the precondition and boundary table first, keep the method deterministic, and do not print.

Treat the three parameters in order as database, queue, shuttingDown. The graded helper cannot verify service draining or orchestration.
hints: Combine the three boolean parameters with a single condition: both dependencies must be true and shuttingDown must be false for READY.
Check the case where every dependency is healthy but shuttingDown is true; that must still yield NOT_READY.

exercises.title: Readiness during shutdown
exercises.instructionMarkdown: The supplied readiness check only looks at database and queue health and ignores shuttingDown entirely, so a draining instance still reports READY. Repair the condition so the program writes exactly `NOT_READY`. Preserve the demonstrated readiness logic and explain why your fix changes the result; do not replace it with a hard-coded print. Output tests verify the result; preserving the intended readiness behavior requires source review.
hints: Readiness must reject new traffic during shutdown.

exercises.title: Secure task-import boundary
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement SecureImport.run(String input). Each nonblank line is id|title|secret, with exactly three fields. Trim fields. id must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,20}; title must contain 1..40 ASCII characters from [A-Za-z0-9 _-]; secret must be nonempty ASCII letters/digits only. Accept at most three unique records. For each accepted record output id|title|redacted where secret length <=4 becomes *** and longer secrets become *** plus their final four characters. Duplicate IDs, oversized/invalid fields, extra delimiters, or records past the capacity emit ERROR. Reject without consuming capacity or retaining an ID. Empty input returns an empty string. This bounded boundary exercise does not substitute for external framework, persistence, and security integration tests.
hints: Parse and validate all fields before mutating state. Split with a negative limit when empty fields must be preserved.
Choose collections according to identity and ordering requirements. Build output lines and join them with a newline.

exercises.title: Task-service command core
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement TaskService.run(String input) as an in-memory command processor. Process nonblank trimmed lines; split on | preserving empty fields and trim every field. Commands: ADD|id|title creates an OPEN task and prints OK; DONE|id marks it DONE and prints OK (repeating DONE is allowed); REMOVE|id removes an existing task and prints OK; LIST prints tasks by ascending numeric ID as id:status:title separated by semicolons, or EMPTY; STATS prints OPEN=<n>,DONE=<n>. IDs must be positive ints; title must be nonempty and contain neither pipe nor semicolon. Invalid syntax, duplicate ADD, unknown commands, invalid IDs, or missing tasks for DONE/REMOVE print ERROR and preserve state. Empty input returns empty text. Each command produces exactly one output line, joined with \n and no trailing newline. Separate domain state from Main and keep each invocation independent. After this graded core, complete the external portfolio in projects/final-capstone.json; the core cannot assess JDBC, HTTP, deployment, or authorization.

exercises.title: Portfolio checkpoint: rollback target selector
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement RollbackSelector.run(String input) as the pure decision core behind the Capstone Deployment Exercise project. Each nonblank trimmed line is one command; blank lines are skipped and produce no output line. DEPLOY|version|healthy requires version to match [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,20} and healthy to be exactly the string true or false; appends this deployment to an ordered history (the same version may be deployed more than once) and prints OK, or ERROR if healthy is neither true nor false. ROLLBACK_TARGET prints the version of the most recent deployment recorded strictly BEFORE the last deployment in history whose healthy value was true, or NONE if no earlier deployment was healthy (including when history has zero or one entries). The last deployment's own healthy value is irrelevant to this query; only entries strictly before it are considered. HISTORY prints every recorded deployment in order as version:healthy separated by semicolons, or EMPTY if none have been recorded. Output is one line per nonblank input line, joined with \n, no trailing newline. This models only the rollback-selection decision; the real Docker build, compose file, and health-check wiring are external, self-directed scope.
hints: "Strictly before the last deployment" excludes the last entry itself even when its own healthy value is true.
Search backward from the second-to-last entry for the most RECENT healthy one, not simply the first one in the whole history.
